messages.subject: Re: CANOPY question
parts:
Hi Jonathan,

Do you have total copy number calls? If you are performing situations, can you generate fractional allele-specific copy numbers? Canopy takes as input fractional allele-specific copy number, the signal of which is mixed with purity and ploidy (we don’t estimate purity and ploidy from the copy number estimate step and defer this to Canopy). Another way is to focus on point mutations only however we don’t think this is the major contribution of Canopy.

Feel free to let me know if you have further questions.

Yuchao

messages.subject: Re: CANOPY question
parts:
Hi Jonathan,

Sorry for my late reply! See my answer below.

It means the allele-specific copy numbers which are fractions due to cancer heterogeneity. Let’s say in this bulk sample you have 10% normal cells, 40% cancer subclone 1 with homozygous deletion and 50% cancer subclone 2 with heterozygous deletion. Then the major copy is  1*10% + 0*40% + 1 * 50% = 0.6 and the minor copy is 1*10% + 0*40% + 0*50% = 0.1

How to generate data input can be found here https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/SNA_CNA_input.md

Yuchao
